PullRequest.Title: sessions: Open Remote workspace submenu on click
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- add an opt-in action-list item behavior that opens a submenu when its parent row is clicked
- enable the behavior for the consolidated workspace picker's **Remote** row
- preserve primary-click behavior for actionable rows that also expose secondary submenu options
- add regression coverage for the shared action list and workspace picker item configuration

Fixes #336172

## Validation

- `npm run transpile-client`
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/platform/actionWidget/browser/actionList.ts src/vs/platform/actionWidget/test/browser/actionList.test.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/browser/sessionWorkspacePicker.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/sessionWorkspacePicker.test.ts`
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/actionWidget/test/browser/actionList.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/sessionWorkspacePicker.test.ts`

Scenarios.Scenario: Mouse click on the consolidated workspace picker's Remote row
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The list selection callback clears selection and calls _showSubmenuForItem, which synchronously converts the already-materialized remote actions into submenu items, constructs a virtualized ActionListWidget, measures/layouts it, and displays it before the interaction completes. If focus or hover already opened this same row, _currentSubmenuElement short-circuits duplicate construction.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective submenu cardinality is the already-grouped union of remote recent workspaces, remote browse actions, remote providers, and contributed remote menu actions; one widget is created per transition from closed/different row to this row.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single synchronous UI-event path; no queued or parallel expensive work. Repeated clicks on the currently open row are coalesced by the current-element guard.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Remote action descriptors are built once when the parent picker is shown. The submenu widget is retained while that row remains open, disposed when cleared, and rebuilt on a later reopen so current action state is reflected; the diff does not alter this lifecycle.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed branch and the synchronous submenu construction/layout call path are directly visible, as is the duplicate-open guard and disposal path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The synchronous cost grows with the number of remote recents, browse actions, providers, and contributed menu actions, although width measurement is capped for lists of 50 or more. Real-world list sizes are uncertain, but opening this list is the requested interaction and the same construction path already ran from hover, chevron, and keyboard activation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff intentionally makes row click invoke the existing submenu-opening path, does not multiply work for one activation, and adds no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network boundary to opening the submenu.

Scenarios.Scenario: Touch tap on an opted-in submenu row
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A gesture tap delivered through the existing List selection event now takes the same synchronous submenu construction/layout path as a mouse click instead of continuing to parent selection.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One activation, with synchronous DOM/list work proportional to effective submenu action cardinality.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One synchronous handler per tap. Gesture registration already belongs to the List implementation, and the changed EventType import does not instantiate another Gesture service.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Identical to mouse opening: already-built action descriptors feed one live submenu widget, duplicate opens are skipped, and submenu disposables are cleared on hide or replacement.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the tap type check, List's existing touch dependency, current-element guard, and cleanup store are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Touch prevalence and remote action counts vary, but there is no evidence of repeated tap dispatch or duplicate widget construction for one activation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The new work is the necessary first rendering of the requested submenu on touch, remains bounded to activation, and introduces no expensive external boundary.

Scenarios.Scenario: Activation of non-opted-in rows, toolbar controls, submenu indicators, and selection of a Remote submenu child
Scenarios.CriticalPath: All row selection events perform one event-type comparison and, for mouse/tap activation, bounded closest-ancestor checks. Non-opted-in rows retain their previous dispatch path. Choosing a child still runs that action and then dispatches the mutable parent item, exactly as when the submenu was opened by hover, chevron, or keyboard before this diff.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Execute the chosen contributed command, browse provider action, remote-host management action, or workspace-selection provider flow.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one operation per explicit submenu child selection; action count in the menu does not cause action execution fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same child action path was reachable through the pre-existing hover, chevron, and keyboard submenu-opening mechanisms with the same one-action cardinality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This operation begins only after a child is selected, not when the changed parent-row click opens the submenu.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant work per ordinary row activation; one downstream operation per selected child, independent of total submenu size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous selection routing; any selected child starts at most one existing command/provider operation. The diff adds no fan-out, queue, or concurrency burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache lookup or invalidation changes. Menu and provider action objects are prepared before activation, and existing submenu teardown releases widget/listeners on hide.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed checks are constant per activation and the downstream child dispatch path is unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: DOM ancestor depth for closest() is small and activation frequency is user-paced; provider operation duration varies but its scheduling and cardinality are unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added checks are bounded interaction-path work, while potentially expensive child operations are neither introduced nor moved onto parent-row opening.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all four changed files and all diff pages. The change adds an opt-in activation route to an existing, guarded submenu renderer; it does not introduce repeated construction for one event, unbounded retention, external-boundary fan-out, or a concurrency burst. No performance findings were submitted.
